relevance_note: Case report of a girl (P1) with LAD I and two ITGB2 variants: 'Genetic testing identified two variants in ITGB2'.
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and copied the multi-space ACMG spans from Supplementary Table 2, checked against the text. Table 1 has patients as columns (P1, P2). Table 2 index-child row stacks three variants (two ITGB2, one ALG2) in single cells; ITGB2 variant details for P1 were taken from text, not by position from that row. P2 (sister, died at 17 days) is said to carry 'the ITGB2 deletion' ('CD11a expression was preserved in both patients (P1 and P2) despite the presence of the ITGB2 deletion') but no variant description is printed for her and she is not in Table 2, so her variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'. The maternal cousin's variant is not reported, so no variant row. Figure 2 legend describes the LAD control as 'A female relative previously diagnosed leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I patient'; the paper does not say this is the maternal cousin, so no separate row was created and the cousin's sex is left not reported. Parents described only as 'healthy': no phenotype rows. ALG2 variant recorded for P1 (attributed unambiguously). Ecthyma gangrenosum taken as a necrotic skin ulcer for the checklist; bacteremia not mapped to 'sepsis'; purulent otitis and abscesses not used for 'absence of pus formation' (left not reported). 'normal lymphocyte immunophenotyping' is a whole investigation and excludes nothing specific. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) text says 'normal lymphocyte immunophenotyping' but Table 1 shows T-cell counts above reference and the Discussion reports 'elevated absolute T-cell counts observed in both affected siblings'; (2) Table 2 gives the same genomic position Chr21:46330218 for both c.119_128del and c.700G>A, whereas Supplementary Table 1 gives hg38 chr21:g.44,901,533C>T for c.700G>A (supplement coordinate used for c.700G>A rows; Table 2 coordinate kept for the father's c.119_128del row only); (3) P2 died at 17 days of age yet has immunophenotyping results in Table 1; (4) Introduction calls P1 'a 3-year-old girl' versus '3-year-and-8-month-old' in the case presentation; (5) Table 2 lists P1's ITGB2 variants as 'Detected' while text calls the deletion heterozygous and the genotype compound heterozygous.
